usageNotes: Use this to read a PDM node's active configuration, including TLS cipher settings, HTTP proxy, notification email, and UI language. Requires the System.Audit privilege on the /system path — API tokens are supported. The special value 'localhost' can be used for the node name when targeting the PDM node itself; all returned fields are optional and may be absent if not configured.

examples.summary: Fetch configuration for the PDM node named 'pdm01'

tips: Use 'localhost' as the node value to target the PDM node you are directly connected to without needing its hostname.
All response fields are optional — an unconfigured node returns an empty object, which is valid.
TLS cipher fields ('ciphers-tls-1.2' and 'ciphers-tls-1.3') follow OpenSSL cipher list/ciphersuites syntax respectively; these affect the PDM API server's TLS negotiation.
Pair with the corresponding PUT/POST config endpoint to audit before making changes.
